narration.text: Aha helps turn research into visual explanations. Two portable skills investigate a question and make its mechanism clear.
Aha Research examines evidence and its limits. Aha Explain designs the chosen medium. Your AI host coordinates the work.
Three examples show the range: everyday phenomena, code, and engineering.
Why does Greenland look enormous? On a spherical Mercator map, high latitudes are enlarged. The projection stretches both directions to preserve local angles.
Move Greenland toward the equator by rotating its boundary on the sphere. Its spherical area stays constant; its footprint on this fixed map shrinks.
Next, look inside code. In CPython, adding this grinning face creates a new string with four-byte slots, even for the ASCII prefix. The original remains unchanged.
That face exceeds the two-byte range. But UTF-eight encodes the ASCII prefix one byte each: the added face contributes just four extra bytes.
Finally, an engineering puzzle. A Docker RUN adds a file: a hundred megabytes of illustrative payload enter an immutable layer.
A later RUN hides the path with a whiteout, but the earlier layer retains its bytes.
Create and delete a new temporary file within one RUN instead: that payload never enters the resulting diff.
The existing Git example shows four formats: interactive HTML for exploration, and an infographic for an overview.
Editable slides help you present the reasoning; narrated video shows how the mechanism changes. Each format is composed for its purpose.
Evidence supports the claim. Visuals reveal the mechanism. Aha creates explanations you can follow.
